invariants: On mobile, task-level workflow actions live in the bottom action boundary by default; headers carry title, context, progress and passive status.
A section exposes at most one dominant primary business action.
Dialog task actions live in the dialog footer.
On web, canonical commands may be mirrored through sticky footer, inline action, keyboard shortcut or utility/action toolbar when this materially improves desktop productivity.
Web accelerators must share the same command, permission, busy/disabled, validation, result and error semantics as the canonical action.
Desktop utility toolbars may host search, filter, sort, column, density, refresh, export, print and batch-selection controls without creating a second workflow.
Focus is visible and not obscured.
Modal focus enters the modal boundary and returns to the invoker on close.
Sticky regions must not cover focused controls or validation messages.
Opening search/filter does not destroy the current work context.
Closing restores prior scroll, selection and draft where the underlying entity still exists.
Search, filter, count and results use the same query revision.
A single-choice step may auto-advance only after an authoritative local selection event.
A redundant Next action is omitted in auto-advance steps.
Back restores the prior selected value without inventing a new workflow state.
UI disabled state is not an integrity boundary.
Every write is bound to a stable entity or work key.
Stale responses may not update a different entity or a newer revision.
Retry must converge or surface a conflict; recoverable input is preserved.
Requested, launched, server-committed and business-confirmed are distinct meanings.
Opening a phone, SMS, email or third-party app is not completion.
Verified completion requires an authoritative receipt when the business process depends on completion.
Mobile is not a scaled desktop.
Reading order and task priority remain stable across layout changes.
Bottom actions include safe-area padding and remain reachable with the virtual keyboard.
Ordinary one-dimensional content reflows at high zoom.
Mobile defines the canonical single-panel task surface; desktop may compose multiple equivalent panels side by side.
Web multi-panel composition reduces navigation depth and preserves context without changing panel-internal information or action hierarchy.
As available width decreases, panel count collapses toward the mobile single-panel flow.
Desktop width alone is not sufficient reason to replace card lists with dense tables or bottom task actions with top toolbars.
Desktop may choose a productivity-optimized surface instead of literal multi-panel composition when comparative, relational or bulk work dominates.
Responsive adaptation may change density, composition and interaction accelerators but not canonical workflow, authority, validation, retry or completion semantics.
WCAG 2.2 AA is the minimum conformance target.
Native semantics are preferred; custom widgets implement equivalent APG semantics.
Meaning is not encoded by color alone.
Touch, pointer, keyboard and assistive input reach the same business outcome unless modality is intrinsic.
Canonical values remain locale-neutral while presentation and parsing are localized.
Language and text direction are explicit metadata.
Logical start/end layout is used for directional layout.
Long translated copy may wrap without hiding required meaning or actions.
A visible file-picker action is always available; drag and drop is an enhancement.
Each file has independent validation/upload/result state.
Preview never substitutes for authoritative file validation.
Remove, retry and cancel are keyboard reachable.
Critical information remains inline and is not toast-only.
Loading, empty, error and populated states are distinct.
Status announcements do not steal focus.
Busy is not success.
IME composition events do not trigger destructive validation, submission or auto-advance.
Virtual keyboards must not hide the focused field or task action boundary.
Input modality does not change completion semantics.
A desktop task panel must remain completable when isolated as the active mobile panel.
Desktop-only affordances are accelerators, not unique business command paths.
A panel may consume stable entity/work context from another panel but may not require a sibling panel to remain visible for correctness.
Required task actions remain in the panel action model and preserve the same command meaning across mobile and web.
Multi-panel collapse preserves entity identity, selection, draft, workflow state and async response ownership.
When multiple panels are visible, prominent Primary actions do not compete without an explicit workflow reason.
Business capability parity is required across mobile and web; identical visual or interaction parity is not.
Desktop grids, bulk actions, inline actions, shortcuts, drag-and-drop alternatives and utility toolbars may accelerate the same canonical commands.
Portable task semantics may be rendered as a non-panel desktop productivity surface when a literal panel would materially reduce efficiency.
Selected, pressed and disabled are exposed through state semantics (aria-pressed, aria-selected, checked, disabled), never by colour or weight alone.
A selectable control keeps one accessible name across states; the name does not flip to the opposite action when the state changes.
Every selectable set declares single or multiple selection, and a required single choice starts from an explicit unselected state.
Selection survives refresh and retry only when bound to a stable entity/work key; it is never silently reassigned.
Focus-visible styling exists for every selectable control and is not removed when a selected style is applied.
